players.product: Niche DRAM (DDR4, DDR3L, LPDDR4X) plus NOR flash and SLC NAND flash (fabless)

quarterly_data.signal: Price outlook (H1 2026 results briefing): board secretary Xie Feiwang and vice chairman and general manager He Wei said niche DRAM prices were still rising at the end of Q2 and are expected to keep rising in H2 at a milder pace; for 2027, limited new DRAM industry capacity means tightness will not ease markedly and prices should fluctuate at a high level. He Wei: SLC NAND Flash shortage has not eased significantly and its upcycle should last at least through all of 2027; NOR Flash mild price rises should continue for some time, more noticeably for high-capacity parts; MCU supply should stay relatively tight for the next few quarters with prices rising mildly. Xie: the company expects high-double-digit MCU revenue growth this year. VP and CFO Sun Guijing: with memory and MCU prices rising mildly and supply-side costs rising, gross margin should gradually reach a relatively stable state.

He Wei (results briefing), citing the 2026 half-year report: at June 30, 2026 the revenue tied to contracted but unfulfilled performance obligations was RMB 97.94 hundred million, of which RMB 94.15 hundred million is to be recognised in H2 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: remaining performance obligations RMB 97.94 hundred million; RMB 94.15 hundred million in H2 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity (results briefing): He Wei said the company expects its DRAM capacity to keep rising over the next few years as its DRAM capacity supplier builds capacity and its own demand for DRAM foundry services grows; NOR Flash capacity should improve well this year with strategic suppliers; SLC NAND capacity is harder to add than NOR Flash, and it is working with suppliers to add it step by step; on the customer side it is considering long-term-agreement-like supply arrangements with core customers; it has no TLC NAND product. Board secretary Xie Feiwang: for customised memory the company is in active talks with strategic partners on 2027 capacity and believes capacity can support 2027 growth.

Customised memory (results briefing): He Wei said subsidiary Qingyun Technology has key customer and project wins in AI phones, AI PCs and robots and is expected to contribute some revenue this year; in 2027, as it reaches mass production at several edge-AI customers, its revenue should grow quickly. Board secretary Xie Feiwang called the 2027 outlook for the business very positive.

MCU drivers (results briefing): board secretary Xie Feiwang said MCUs mainly use mature 90nm-22nm processes, fabs are shifting mature-node capacity to AI-related business (memory, edge SoCs) and packaging and test costs have risen, so MCU supply is tight; demand comes from industrial restocking after two years of destocking (new energy, energy storage), data-center optical modules (in which the MCU is a very important component), digital power for data centers, and new consumer uses such as 3D printing and smart robots, where the company's MCUs gained good results and share. He Wei said H1 2026 MCU revenue growth of 49.07% came mainly from much higher shipments, and NOR Flash volume grew in every application with industrial and automotive revenue and volume up sharply.
